rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly, so the table is tuned up for stronger obfuscation on this small, hot numeric benchmark (5 functions, ~1.8KB text, tight loops in n-body/spectral-norm/fannkuch). FLA and SUB get the highest Security/Diversity weights since control-flow flattening plus arithmetic substitution give the best structural and data-level confusion for such compact functions; BCF and IBR are enabled but with elevated RuntimeCost weights (0.55/0.45) so opaque predicates and branch indirection concentrate on the few larger functions (main, advance, energy) rather than the hottest inner loops; ICALL and IGV add call and global indirection cheaply for RE friction; SPLIT stays cost-cheap and diversity-heavy to fragment the small functions. CorrectnessRisk weights are kept low-to-moderate since round 1 showed no issues, but not zero, preserving a safety margin on the recursive and bit-manipulation code paths. Overall this pushes reverse-engineering resistance well up while keeping runtime and size penalties acceptable for compute-bound benchmark code.
